newsitem.title: USA: New Hampshire eyes hefty cigarette tax hike.
newsitem.headline: New Hampshire eyes hefty cigarette tax hike.

text.p: New Hampshire Gov. Jeanne Shaheen Tuesday asked the Legislature to fast track a bill raising the state's tax on tobacco products to fund public kindergarten, discourage teenage smoking and retire a looming $60 million budget deficit.
Shaheen, a Democrat, said the tax could raise as much as $46 million.
Her budget director, Charles Connor, told the House Finance Committee that the new administration inherited an estimated $37 million deficit from Republican Stephen Merrill.
He added that costs from a mandated share of state Meals and Rooms Tax revenues earmarked to New Hampshire communities should boost the deficit to $60 million.
"These are costs out of our control," Connor said. He asked the Finance Committee to fast track passage of the bill so it can become effective in April.
If lawmakers pass the legislation quickly, New Hampshire could glean $12 million by the end of June to help close its budget deficit, he said.
Connor's testimony came during a House Finance Committee session on the bill, HB 564, which calls for a 20 cent increase of New Hampshire's current tax on cigarettes of 25 cents per pack.
The bill's sponsors Rep. Channing Brown (R-Lebanon) and Rep. Raymond Buckley (D-Manchester) said they welcomed the increase proposed by the administration.
"It will prevent young people from smoking and save lives. It is time to act like statesmen," Buckley said.
New Hampshire currently levies a 25 cent per pack tax on cigarettes which compares to Vermont's 51 cent tax, Maine's 48 cent tax and Massachusetts' 86 cents per pack tax.
